Up to 1936 many tables — the empire censuses and statistical yearbooks above all — print it together with the South Manchuria Railway Zone as one unit (關東州及滿鐵附屬地), often headed just “Kwantung”: those figures are under [[kwantung-zone]], and the zone alone is under [[smr]]. The zone passed to Manchukuo on 1 December 1937, so from 1937 the figures are the territory alone.
pn.kwantung-zone: The leased territory and the South Manchuria Railway Zone counted as one unit, as the empire censuses and statistical yearbooks print them up to 1936 (often headed just 關東州 or “Kwantung”). The territory alone is under [[kwantung]], the zone alone under [[smr]]. The zone passed to Manchukuo on 1 December 1937; from 1937 the tables' 關東州 is the territory alone, listed under [[kwantung]].
pn.smr: The railway zone alone. Figures for the zone together with the leased territory, as most empire-wide tables print them up to 1936, are under [[kwantung-zone]]; the territory alone is under [[kwantung]]. The zone passed to Manchukuo on 1 December 1937.
pn.manchuria: “Manchuria” covers different ground from table to table: before 1932 usually the Three Eastern Provinces (Fengtien or Liaoning, Kirin, Heilungkiang); from 1932 Manchukuo, which added Jehol (taken in 1933) and the Hsingan Mongol provinces; and some tables count the [[kwantung]] and the [[smr]] in while others leave them out (the zone went to Manchukuo in December 1937). Check a table's heading and notes before comparing its figures with another's.
pn.empire: What “the Empire” includes varies. In the census tables the 帝國 total is Japan proper, Korea, Taiwan and Karafuto only (76,988,379 in 1920; 97,697,555 in 1935); the [[kwantung-zone]] and the [[nanyo]] are printed below it. A “grand total” adds them back (99,456,818 in 1935), some tables count Kwantung without the Railway Zone, and the yearly series of the statistical yearbooks add Japan proper's 1 October estimate to the colonies' year-end counts. Check what a table's total covers before comparing it with another's.

empire: Population of Overseas Colonies, 1930–1939 (Statistical Yearbook of Imperial Japan No. 59, Table 3C)
Japan Data Catalog for the Humanities and Social Sciences (JSPS); data distributed by the Institute of Economic Research, Hitotsubashi University
japan: 大正9年国勢調査 (1920 census) and census time series since 1920
Statistics Bureau of Japan, via e-Stat

The first census (1 Oct 1920) as PDF tables by prefecture (area, population by city/district, households); later censuses and the long-run series 'population by sex, nation and prefecture, 1920-2015' are in the same e-Stat census section (e.g. stat_infid=000031524010).
統計150年 特設サイト: 統計史 (digitised census and yearbook reports)
Statistical-history pages linking to the digitised 1920 census report (national volumes and prefectural volumes, 1920-1928) at the National Diet Library, and to other early statistical publications.
人口統計資料集 (Latest Demographic Statistics), Table 1-1
National Institute of Population and Social Security Research (IPSS)

Total population of Japan proper from 1872 (mostly estimates before 1920; census figures from 1920), with natural increase and migration; the annual data book also has long series by prefecture, age and sex.
日本帝国統計年鑑 (digitised yearbook volumes)
Yearbook No. 58 (1939) as an example of the digitised run (Nos. 39-59); population chapters give census and registration-based counts for Japan proper by prefecture.
korea: Census population trends, 1925-1949 (Population Policy, Yesterday and Today)
Statistics Korea (via National Archives of Korea theme site)
Table of total, male and female population and sex ratio for the census years 1925, 1930, 1935, 1940, 1944 and 1949.
Institute of Economic Research, Hitotsubashi University

Long-term series of macro-economic, population and labour-force statistics for Korea from the 1910s, as downloadable tables (companion to the published volume); the page does not itemise the population tables.
taiwan: 臺灣日治時期統計資料庫 (Taiwan Colonial Statistics Database)

About 684 volumes of colonial-period statistical books (e.g. the Government-General statistical yearbooks and census volumes) browsable by title or subject, with page images and table metadata; population (戶口) tables are among the 29 categories. Open access. Check at 2026-11-09: server answered HTTP 200 to curl; a fetch tool was refused connection once.
Institute of Economic Research, Hitotsubashi University
Long-term statistical series for Taiwan from the colonial period on, as downloadable tables (companion to the published volume), including population.
日本統治時期臺灣省五十一年來統計提要 (1894-1945)
Taiwan Provincial Government Statistical Office (1946), digitised by Academia Sinica
1946 compilation of 51 years of Taiwan statistics, 24 subject areas including population; viewable and downloadable. Text quality of the scan is uneven.
Program for Historical Demography, Academia Sinica

Individual-level colonial household registers; the open-access Historical Life Course Studies article describes the database and its use. The data themselves require an application to the programme (not freely downloadable). Link is to the description, not the data.
karafuto: Population of Overseas Colonies, 1930–1939 (Statistical Yearbook of Imperial Japan No. 59, Table 3C, South Sakhalin column)
Japan Data Catalog for the Humanities and Social Sciences (JSPS); data distributed by the Institute of Economic Research, Hitotsubashi University
Resident population of South Sakhalin year-end 1930-1939 within the overseas-territories table; other records cover earlier years.
nanyo: Population of Overseas Colonies, 1930–1939 (Statistical Yearbook of Imperial Japan No. 59, Table 3C, South Seas Mandate column)
Japan Data Catalog for the Humanities and Social Sciences (JSPS); data distributed by the Institute of Economic Research, Hitotsubashi University
Mandate population 1 Oct each year 1930-1937, then year-end 1938-1939; other records in the series give 1920s figures.
china: Institute of Economic Research, Hitotsubashi University (COE Newsletter No. 9)

Scholarly review of the Republican-era surveys (1912, 1928, 1936) and of methods for re-estimating pre-1949 population; cites the Hitotsubashi COE discussion paper 'Republican Population: A Review' (1997).
Institute of Economic Research, Hitotsubashi University

Long-term annual series for 1912-2020 for the area governed by the PRC as of 2013 (excludes Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macau); the page does not itemise which tables hold population, so check the contents file.
world: Groningen Growth and Development Centre, University of Groningen

Long-run comparative economic database for 169 countries (Excel and Stata downloads); the data files carry population alongside GDP per capita, but the page itself does not state the population series or start years.
Downloadable country total-population series, 1500-2000 (50-year steps to 1800, then decennial), on today's country list.
Our World in Data: Population data sources
Explains the long-run population series by country (HYDE to 1799, Gapminder v7 for 1800-1949 built on Maddison and Clio Infra, UN from 1950), all on today's borders.

tn.china: The population of the Republic of China before 1949 is notoriously difficult to estimate. Be sure to explore the scholarship around the challenges before making use of any of these statistics.
